channel.title: Signal
channel.description: Tech news matched to Patrick's interests, curated daily.

item.title: Infini-AI-Lab releases Hermit, an open-source harness adapter framework for AI agents
item.description: Hermit trains a small external adapter that tunes Codex or Claude Code agents to new tasks while leaving both the model and the harness frozen, with local vLLM, SGLang, or Ollama backends.

item.title: October 2026 Developer Update
item.description: The Forge's October update recaps its livestream: V14 builds 368 and 369 now available, a demo of Game Environments keeping per-game Foundry setups separate, and a new free BGK board game, reVAMP.

item.title: MCP Suite Pro v1.0.2 aligns LM Studio and Ollama timeouts for large local models
item.description: Small devlog release standardizing local-model timeouts at 300 seconds so heavy quantized weights (14B-70B) finish loading into VRAM without premature HTTP aborts, plus env-var controls for the LM Studio, Ollama, and chat timeouts.

item.title: Cognitum One Unveils MetaHarness, an Open-Source Factory for Agent Harnesses
item.description: Announced at GitHub Universe 2026, MetaHarness generates a branded, governed coding-agent harness from a repo or blank page, with its own CLI, MCP server, scoped memory, and signed releases, while the model stays swappable.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows reaches general availability
item.description: GitHub's open-source project for automating reasoning-based tasks with coding agents inside Actions is now generally available, compiling natural-language Markdown workflow definitions into standard Actions YAML with sandboxed, read-only-by-default execution.

item.title: WoW Forever aims for four-month raid tiers and PC gamepad support at launch
item.description: Blizzard plans a roughly four-month patch rhythm with raid tiers and PvP seasons about three times a year, plus PC gamepad support, while keeping the launch focus on Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor.

item.title: Stop Buying GPUs: Turn Your Phone Into eGPU For Local AI
item.description: A walkthrough of running llama.cpp in Termux so an Android phone serves as an offline local AI backend for a PC over USB, including which model sizes fit phone RAM.

item.title: Dataiku launches Headless for agentic coding tools
item.description: Dataiku's new Headless capability lets coding agents build, migrate, and inspect governed data projects from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and similar tools without leaving the editor.

item.title: Small, Fast, Local: MTS AI's Cotype Nano Arrives on Modelers.cn
item.description: A GGUF build of MTS AI's compact Cotype Nano model lands on Modelers.cn, giving llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio users a lightweight local option.

item.title: Codein v1.0.7: lightweight Termux AI terminal agent gets easier to launch
item.description: Termux-based terminal agent launcher update adding AI provider support and chat history, aimed at running AI-assisted terminal workflows on Android devices and modest hardware.

item.title: Epic VTT beta update: repairs and December 1 launch goal
item.description: Browser-based VTT Epic VTT reports beta progress on campaign persistence, multiplayer sync, and permissions as it holds a December 1 public-launch target.

item.title: Llama Guard 3 1B goes local as a GGUF build
item.description: A community GGUF conversion of Meta's 1.2B-parameter Llama Guard 3 safety classifier, packaged for llama.cpp so prompt and output screening can run fully on-device — though it is a mirrored conversion, not an official Meta release.

item.title: OllamaServer: one-click Ollama on Android, no Termux needed
item.description: A new Android app starts the Ollama service with one tap, pulls official models, and accepts custom GGUF uploads, removing the Termux setup step for on-device inference.

item.title: SuperNova-Lite reasoning model arrives as GGUF for local runs
item.description: A community GGUF packaging of Arcee AI's 8B SuperNova-Lite, a DeepSeek-R1-distilled reasoner, sized to run on consumer hardware at roughly 5-6 GB in 4-bit.

item.title: Lang-Exster 0.5B Instruct lands in ONNX for tiny on-device use
item.description: A half-billion-parameter Apache-2.0 instruction model exported to ONNX for portable CPU and edge inference, with a conversion path to Huawei Ascend NPUs.

item.title: Liquid AI's compact LFM2-2.6B-Exp gets a GGUF build for edge testing
item.description: A llama.cpp-compatible GGUF conversion of Liquid AI's experimental 2.6B hybrid-attention model, aimed at evaluating the LFM2 family on CPUs, Apple Silicon, and consumer GPUs.

item.title: Liquid AI releases LFM3, six small open-weight models for local hardware
item.description: Six roughly 2B-parameter models covering text, vision, audio and decision tasks, with llama.cpp built from source as the fastest local route and the tiny text model reaching about 40 tokens per second on CPU in testing.

item.title: DevQuasar's Llama 3.2 3B GGUF lands on Modelers.cn for local inference
item.description: A GGUF packaging of Meta's 3B Llama 3.2 model for offline text generation on laptops and constrained devices via llama.cpp-compatible runtimes, with no Ascend-specific optimization on the card.

item.title: Tiny LLM, Giant Context: Menlo's Lucy-128k Now Available on Modelers.cn
item.description: Menlo Research's Lucy-128k arrives as a GGUF build with a 128k-token context window, aimed at long-document local research agents.

item.title: LocoOperator 4B GGUF lands on Modelers.cn
item.description: A community GGUF conversion of a small 4B operator-style model, packaged for llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio, though its model card lists no benchmarks or clear provenance.

item.title: Axolotl v0.21.0 adds fine-tuning support for Reflection's Beam
item.description: Axolotl's latest release ships Beam support with QLoRA on a single 8xH200 node, FSDP2 configs and expert-parallel LoRA recipes for B200 GPUs.

item.title: LM Studio vs Ollama vs llama.cpp (2026): Speed and Setup
item.description: A freshly updated rundown of the local-runner landscape: Ollama is back on llama.cpp's llama-server for GGUF models with MLX as the Apple Silicon default, and LM Studio's 0.4.0 line no longer needs the desktop app installed.

item.title: Hobbyists are squeezing trillion-parameter models onto laptops
item.description: Quantization and SSD streaming let hobbyists run enormous open-weight models on consumer rigs and MacBooks, slowly if at all fast, as the floor for serious local inference keeps dropping.

item.title: Lucie-7B Goes GGUF: A French Open LLM You Can Now Run Locally
item.description: OpenLLM-France's French-oriented 7B instruct model repackaged in GGUF, so it runs through llama.cpp-style runtimes on a laptop or workstation without a full Transformers setup.

item.title: Agensh's real lesson is the coordination layer, not the swarm
item.description: A builder's read on Agensh: copy its shared workspace rules, task claiming, and merge handling as infrastructure, rather than chasing thousand-agent swarms as the default.

item.title: Microsoft open-sources Agensh, a leaderless harness for 1,024 coding agents
item.description: Microsoft Research's Agensh drops the lead agent entirely: every worker runs the same claim-act-verify-merge loop over a shared workspace, scaling from one to 1,024 agents in tests.

item.title: Microsoft open-sources Agensh, a leaderless harness scaling to 1,024 coding agents
item.description: Microsoft Research's MIT-licensed Agensh drops the central orchestrator: workers claim sub-tasks, share findings, and merge through a shared workspace, with reported pass-rate gains as agent counts scale.

item.title: Microsoft Open-Sources Agensh, a Multi-Agent Harness for 1,024 Agents
item.description: Microsoft Research released a leaderless coding-agent harness where workers claim their own subtasks and merge into a shared repo, scaling from 1 to 1,024 agents on ProgramBench.

item.title: Microsoft open-sources Agensh, a leaderless 1,024-agent coding harness
item.description: Microsoft Research releases a decentralized coding harness where workers claim their own subtasks and merge into a shared repo, scaled to 1,024 agents in its ProgramBench tests.

item.title: Old Galaxy phone as a local LLM host: Termux works, but only in the foreground
item.description: A Galaxy S23 FE runs Gemma 4 E2B through Termux llama.cpp at usable speeds only while the app stays visible; backgrounded, Android throttles it to three cores and about 0.1 tok/s, a quirk fixed by running Termux and Chrome in split-screen.

item.title: Microsoft open-sources Agensh, a decentralized harness for up to 1,024 agents
item.description: Microsoft Research's decentralized harness drops the central orchestrator: workers claim their own subtasks, share findings, and merge into a common Git repo, scaling in tests to 1,024 agents on ProgramBench.

item.title: AI This Week: open tools for safer agents
item.description: Weekly roundup of open agent tooling, including Google's self-refining Harness² framework, big jumps in COBOL-migration benchmarks, and new open infrastructure for safer agents.

item.title: Flint AI: Recursive's open-weight coding model for laptops
item.description: Recursive's Flint ships Apache-2.0 open weights tuned for laptops rather than servers, with OpenHands supporting it through OpenRouter or a local endpoint from release day.

item.title: TanStack AI 1.0 ships a stable, provider-agnostic agent toolkit
item.description: TanStack AI reaches 1.0 with stable agent, subagent, and MCP APIs across 76 packages, plus an experimental multi-environment harness.

item.title: llama.cpp --n-cpu-moe: a 35B MoE model at readable speed on an 8GB laptop GPU
item.description: Offloading the first 28 layers' MoE expert weights to system RAM with llama.cpp's --n-cpu-moe flag lifted a 35B MoE model from about 4 to about 33 tokens per second on an 8GB laptop GPU, keeping attention, embeddings and KV cache in VRAM.

item.title: You.com launches Inference Router for open-weight models with enterprise SLAs
item.description: New routing service sends requests to open-weight models served by Parasail, Inception, Meta and Alibaba Cloud under enterprise SLAs; early customers report roughly halved inference bills.

item.title: Ling-3.0-tiny DFlash draft for stock llama.cpp
item.description: A community builder extracted the draft-head from a Ling-3.0-tiny UBTree release so it runs on stock llama.cpp via dflash speculative decoding, reporting roughly 8% faster prose and 61% faster code generation.

item.title: AMD's New ONNX Phi-3.5 Mini: A Local AI Powerhouse for Ryzen AI Laptops
item.description: Modelers.cn published a 4-bit ONNX build of Microsoft's Phi-3.5-mini tuned for AMD Ryzen AI 300-series NPUs, shrinking the model to a 2-3GB footprint for fully on-device inference on Strix Point laptops.

item.title: Lumabri shards LLM inference across local machines in pure C
item.description: A new open-source tool splits model layers across several household computers so a model too big for one machine's RAM can still run fully locally, with each machine approving its share before anything loads.

item.title: WoW Forever adds a Roleplay-PvP ruleset at launch
item.description: Blizzard will offer a Roleplay-PvP ruleset when WoW Forever launches November 4, with name reservations opening October 27.
